en: Man as an individual relates himself to himself.
He has the twofold side of his particularity and his universal essence.
His duty toward himself is insofar partly his physical preservation, partly [this] to raise his individual being to his universal nature, to form himself.
zh: 人作为个体与自身相关。
他有他的个别性和他的一般本质的双重方面。
他对自己的义务，就此而言一部分是他身体的保存，一部分是［这一点］：把它的个别存在者提升到其一般本性上去，即进行自我教养。

en: Explanation.
Man is on the one hand a natural being.
As such he behaves according to arbitrariness and chance, as an unstable, subjective being.
He does not distinguish the essential from the non-essential. - Secondly, he is a spiritual, rational being.
According to this side he is not by nature what he should be.
The animal requires no cultivation, for it is by nature what it should be.
It is only a natural being.
Man, however, must bring his twofold side into agreement, make his particularity conform to his rational side, or make the latter the ruling one.

Man is uneducated, for example, when he gives way to his anger and acts blindly in accordance with this affect, because in it he takes an insult or injury to be an infinite injury and seeks to make it up by injuring the offender or other objects without measure and aim. - He is uneducated if someone asserts an interest that is of no concern to him, or in which he can achieve nothing by his activity, since one can sensibly make something one’s interest only where one brings something about by one’s activity. - Further, if man becomes impatient at the encounters of fate, he makes his particular interest into a matter of the highest importance, as something which men and circumstances ought to have accommodated themselves to.
zh: 诠释。
人首先是一个自然存在物。
作为这样的存在物，他按照任意和偶然行事，是一个不稳定的、主观的存在物。
他不把本质性的东西与非本质性的东西区分开来。——其次，他是一个精神的、有理性的存在物。
就这一面而言，他并不是依其本性就是他所应是的东西。
动物不需要教养，因为它依其本性就是它所应是的东西。
它只是一个自然存在物。
但人必须使他的双重方面彼此相合，使他的个别性符合于他理性的一面，或者使后者成为起支配作用的方面。

例如，当人听任自己的怒气发作、盲目地顺着这种情感行事时，他就是未受教养的，因为在这种情况下他把一项侮辱或伤害看成无限的伤害，并且企图不加限度与目标地通过对冒犯者或其他对象的伤害来补偿它。——当某人主张一种与他毫不相干、或者他通过自己的行动根本无法产生效果的利害关系时，他也是未受教养的，因为按理说，人只能在自己通过行动能做成某事的地方，才把那件事变成自己的利害关系。——此外，当人遇到命运的安排而变得不耐烦时，他就把自己特殊的利害关系变成了极其重要的事，好像是人们和情境本应当迁就于它似的。

en: To theoretical cultivation belongs, besides the multiplicity and determinacy of the cognitions and the universality of the viewpoints from which things are to be judged, a sense for the objects in their free independence, without a subjective interest.
zh: 理论的教养除了知识的丰富与规定性、以及据以评判事物的观点的普遍性之外，还包括对对象在其自由独立性方面的感觉，即不带主观的利害关系。

en: Explanation.

The multiplicity of cognitions as such belongs to cultivation, because man thereby raises himself from the particular knowledge of insignificant things of the environment to a general knowledge, through which he attains a greater commonality of knowledge with other men, comes into possession of generally interesting objects.
Insofar as man goes beyond what he immediately knows and experiences, he learns that there are also other and better ways of behaving and acting, and that his own is not the only necessary one.

He withdraws from himself and comes to the distinction of the essential and the non-essential. - The determinacy of cognitions concerns the essential difference of them, the differences that belong to the objects under all circumstances.
To cultivation belongs a judgment about the relations and objects of reality.
For this it is necessary that one know what is at stake, what the nature and the purpose of a thing and of the relations to one another are.
These viewpoints are not given immediately through contemplation, but through occupation with the thing, through reflection on its purpose and essence and on the means, how far the same reach or not.
The uneducated man stays at immediate contemplation.
He has no open eye and does not see what lies before his feet.
It is only a subjective seeing and apprehension.
He does not see the thing.

He knows only roughly what it is like, and not even that correctly, because only the knowledge of the general viewpoints guides to what one must consider essential, or because it already is the most important thing about the thing itself, already contains its most excellent aspects, into which one therefore only has so to speak to lay the external determinate being, and so one is able to apprehend it much more easily and correctly.
zh: 诠释。
知识本身的丰富多样属于教养，因为人由此从对周围无足轻重之物的特殊知识提升到一种普遍知识，通过这种知识他与他人达到更大的知识共同性，并获得对普遍上有趣的对象的占有。
当人越出他直接知道和经历的东西时，他就学到行为与行动还有别的和更好的方式，而他自己那一种并不是唯一必要的方式。
他从自身退开，进而达到对本质性的与非本质性的区分。——知识的规定性涉及它们本质上的差别，即在一切情况下都属于对象的那些差别。
教养还包括对现实性的关系与对象的判断。
为此所需要的是：人应当知道关键何在，知道一件事物以及彼此关系各自的本性和目的是什么。
这些观点并不是通过直观直接给予的，而是通过对该事物的处理、对它的目的与本质以及对其效力所及与否的手段的思考而得到的。
未受教养的人停留在直接直观上。
他没有敞开的眼睛，看不见就在他脚前的东西。
那只是一种主观的观看与把握。
他看不见事情本身。
他只是大致知道这件事物是怎样的，而且连这也并不确切，因为只有对普遍观点的知识才能引向人必须作本质性考察的东西；或者因为它本身就已经是这件事物最主要的东西，已经包含着它最优越的方面，因此人只需要仿佛把外在的定在放进这些方面里去就行，于是也就更能轻易而正确地把握它。

en: The opposite of not knowing how to judge is that one judges hastily about everything without understanding it.
Such a hasty judgment is founded on the fact that one does indeed grasp a viewpoint, but a one-sided one, and thereby overlooks the true concept of the thing, the remaining viewpoints.
A cultivated man also knows the limit of his judgement.
zh: 与「不懂得判断」相反的，是不加理解就对一切匆忙下判断。
这种匆忙的判断建立在这样一点上：人确实抓住了一个观点，却是一个片面的观点，因而就忽略了事情真正的概念、忽略了其余的观点。
一个有教养的人同时知道自己判断能力的界限。

en: Furthermore, to cultivation belongs a sense for the objective in its freedom.

It lies in this, that I do not seek my particular subject in the object, but consider and treat the objects as they are in and for themselves in their free peculiarity, that I take an interest in them without a particular benefit. - Such an unselfish interest lies in the study of the sciences, namely when one cultivates them for their own sake.
The desire to draw benefit from the objects of nature is connected with their destruction. - The interest in beautiful art is also an unselfish one.

It represents things in their living independence and leaves out the paltry and stunted as they suffer from external circumstances. - The objective action consists in this, that 1. it also has with respect to its indifferent side the form of the universal, free of arbitrariness, mood and caprice, from the extraordinary and the like; 2. with respect to its inner, essential side it is objective when one has the true thing itself as one’s purpose, without self-interested interest.
zh: 此外，教养还包括对客观事物之自由的感受力。
它在于：我不去对象中寻找我的特殊主体，而是按照对象自在自为的样子、在它们自由的特性上去观察和处理它们，也就是说不带任何特殊的利害关系去关心它们。——这样的无私利害关系就在对科学的研究中：当人正是为科学自身而研究它的时候。
要从自然的对象中谋取利益的欲求，是与它们的破坏联系在一起的。——对美的艺术的利害关系同样是一种无私的。
它把事物以其活的独立性表现出来，并把那些因外在情境而受损的贫乏与萎缩之物略去。——客观的行为在于：1. 它即使就其无所谓的一面而言也具有普遍者的形式，摆脱了任意、情绪和怪癖，摆脱了特殊之类的东西；2. 就其内在的、本质的一面而言，当人把事情的真身本身当作自己的目的而不带自利的利害关系时，它就是客观的。

en: To practical cultivation belongs that man show that composure and moderation in the satisfaction of natural needs and drives which lies within the limits of their necessity, namely self-preservation.

He must 1. be free of the natural, of it; 2. on the contrary, in his vocation, in the essential, he must be [deeply engaged], and therefore 3. he must be able not only to restrict the satisfaction of the natural to the limits of necessity, but also to sacrifice it to higher duties.
zh: 实践的教养包括：人在满足自然的需要与冲动时，表现出那种处在其必然性的界限之内、亦即自我保存的清醒与节制。
他必须 1. 从自然的东西中走出来，摆脱它；2. 相反，在自己的职业中、在本质性的事情上，他必须深入，并且因此 3. 不仅要把对自然之物的满足限制在必然性的界限之内，还要能够把它牺牲给更高的义务。

en: Explanation.

Man’s freedom from natural drives does not consist in the fact that he has none and so does not strive to escape his nature, but in the fact that he acknowledges them as such as something necessary and thereby rational and accomplishes them accordingly with his will.
He finds himself compelled in this only insofar as he sets up random and arbitrary impulses and purposes against the universal.
The determinate, exact measure in the satisfaction of needs and in the use of physical and spiritual powers cannot be indicated exactly, but everyone can know what is useful or harmful to him.

Moderation in the satisfaction of natural drives and in the use of bodily powers is necessary as such for the sake of health, for health is an essential condition for the use of spiritual powers for the fulfillment of man’s higher determination.

If the body is not preserved in its ordinary condition, if it is injured in one of its functions, one must make it the purpose of one’s activity, whereby it becomes something dangerous and significant for the spirit. - Furthermore, exceeding the measure in the use of physical and spiritual powers has as a consequence, either through too much or too little, a blunting and weakening of them.
zh: 诠释。
人摆脱自然冲动的自由，不在于他没有自然冲动、因而不谋求逃离自己的本性，而在于他总体上把它们承认为某种必然的、因而也是合乎理性的东西，并以自己的意志相应地完成它们。
他只在把偶然的和任意的念头与目的同普遍者相对立这一点上，才感到自己受约束。
在满足需要和使用身体与精神力量时那个确定而精确的分寸，是无法精确指出的，但每个人都能知道什么对自己有益、什么有害。
在满足自然冲动和使用身体力量时的节制，总体上出于健康的缘故是必要的，因为健康是运用精神力量以实现人的更高规定的一个本质条件。
如果身体没有保持在它的正常状态、如果它的某一项功能受到损害，人就必须把身体当作自己活动的目的，这样它就成为对精神来说某种危险而重大的东西。——此外，在使用身体与精神力量时越过分寸，无论是过多还是过少，都会导致这些力量的迟钝与虚弱。

en: Finally, moderation is connected with composure.

This consists in the consciousness of what one does, that man surveys himself through his reflection in the enjoyment or in the work, and so is not wholly surrendered to this individual state, but remains open to the consideration of something else, which may also still be necessary.
In composure one is out of one’s state, of the sensation or of the business, together with the spirit.
This position of not sinking completely into one’s state is as such required with regard to drives and purposes which are indeed necessary but not essential in the process.
On the contrary, with regard to a true purpose or business the spirit must be present with its whole earnestness and not at the same time be outside of it.
Composure here consists in one’s having all the circumstances and sides of the work before one’s eyes.
zh: 最后，节制与清醒是相联系的。
这种清醒在于对自己正在做的事有所意识：人在享受或工作中通过反思审视自己，因此并不完全沉溺于这一个别的状态，而是对「别的东西——它也许同样还是必要的」保持敞开。
在清醒中，人连同精神一起，从自己的状态、从感觉或从所办之事中抽身出来。
这种「不完全沉入自己状态」的姿态，总体上对于那些固然必要、但在此过程中并非本质性的冲动和目的来说是必需的。
相反，对于真正的目的或事业，精神必须以全部的认真在场，而不能同时又置身于它之外。
这里的清醒在于：人把工作的一切情境和各个侧面都看在眼里。

en: As for the determinate vocation which appears as a fate, the form of an external necessity is to be lifted from it as such.
One is to take it up with freedom and to endure and carry it out in such freedom.
zh: 至于那个显得像是命运的规定了的职业，总体上要扬弃掉加在它身上的外在必然性的形式。
要用自由去着手于它，并以这样的自由去坚持和完成它。

en: Explanation.

Man, with a view to the external circumstances of fate and to everything of which he is at all immediately the being, must behave in such a way that he makes the same his own, that he takes from it the form of an external determinate being.
It does not depend in which external state man finds himself through fate, if he is right in what he is, i.e. if he fills out all sides of his vocation.
The vocation to an estate is a many-sided substance.
It is as it were a stuff or material which he must work through in all directions, so that it has in it nothing alien, brittle, and resistant.
Insofar as I have made it completely mine for myself, I am free in it.
Man is especially discontented when he does not fill out his vocation.
He gives himself a relation which he does not truly have as his own.
At the same time he belongs to this estate.
He cannot rid himself of it.
He thus lives and acts in a relation with himself that is contrary to his will.
zh: 诠释。
就命运的外部情境以及他直接所是的一切而言，人必须这样行事：他把它变成自己的东西，他从中取消了外在定在的形式。
人在命运中处于哪一种外在状态并不重要，只要他把自己所是的东西做对，即只要他把自己职业的所有方面都填满。
一个提升到某种地位的职业是一种多方面的实体。
它仿佛是一种材料，他必须朝各个方向把它彻底加工透，好使它其中不再有任何陌生的、脆硬的和抵触的东西。
只要我已把它完完全全地变成我自己的东西，我就在其中是自由的。
人在没有填满自己的职业时，特别会感到不满。
他给自己一个关系，而他并没有真正把它当作自己的东西。
同时他又属于这个地位。
他无法从中摆脱出来。
于是他就生活在并行动于一种令他自己反感的自我关系之中。

en: Fidelity and obedience in one’s vocation, as well as obedience toward fate and self-forgetfulness in one’s acting, have as their ground the giving up of vanity, self-conceit and self-seeking against what is in and for itself and necessary.
zh: 职业中的忠诚与服从、对命运的服从以及行动中的自我遗忘，其根据在于放弃那虚荣、自负与自私对自在自为而必然之物的抗拒。

en: Explanation.
The vocation is something universal and necessary and makes up some side of human life in common.
It is thus a part of the whole work of humanity.
When man has a vocation, he enters into participation and cooperation in the universal.
He thereby becomes something objective.
The vocation is indeed a single, limited sphere, yet it makes up a necessary member of the whole and is also in itself again a whole.
If man is to become something, he must know how to limit himself, i.e. to make his vocation entirely his concern.
Then it is no limitation for him.
He is then at one with himself, with his externality, with his sphere.

He is something universal, a whole. - If man makes something vain to himself, i.e. something non-essential and trivial, his purpose, then what lies at the basis here is not an interest in a thing but in his own thing.
The vain is nothing existing in and for itself, but is preserved only through the subject.

Man sees in this only himself; e.g. there can also be a moral vanity when man in his acting is at all conscious of his excellence and has the interest more in himself than in the thing. - The man who faithfully accomplishes small tasks shows himself capable of greater ones, because he has shown obedience, a giving up of his wishes, inclinations, and fancies.
zh: 诠释。
职业是某种普遍而必然的东西，它构成人共同生活中的一面。
所以它是整个人类作品的一部分。
当人有了职业，他就是参与并协作于普遍者。
他由此成为一个客观的东西。
职业固然是一个个别的、受限制的领域，但它构成整体的一个必要环节，而且它自身又是一个整体。
如果人应当成为某种东西，他就必须懂得限制自己，也就是完完全全地把自己的职业当作自己的事情。
那么它对他就不再是界限。
于是他就与自身、与他的外在性、与他的领域合而为一。
他是一个普遍者、一个整体。——当人把某种虚妄的东西，即某种非本质的、琐屑的东西当作自己的目的时，这时所依据的并不是对某件事物的利害关系，而是对他自己的事情的利害关系。
虚妄的东西并不是自在自为地存在着的东西，而只是靠主体才得以维持。
人在其中只看见自己；例如，也可能有道德上的虚荣：当人在行动中总体上意识到自己的卓越，而把利害关系更多地放在自己而非事情上时。——那个忠实地完成小事的人表明自己有能力完成更大的事，因为他表现出了服从，表现出了对自己的愿望、倾向和幻想的放弃。

en: Through intellectual and moral cultivation man acquires the ability to fulfil the duties toward others, which duties can be called real, whereas the duties that relate to cultivation are more of a formal nature.
zh: 通过智性的与道德的教养，人获得履行对他人的义务的能力；这些义务可以称为实在的义务，而那些关涉教养的义务则更具形式的本性。

en: Insofar as the fulfilment of duties appears more as the subjective property of an individual and belongs more to his natural character, it is virtue.
zh: 就义务的履行显得更是一个个体的主观财产、更属于他的自然性情而言，它就是美德。

en: Because virtue is partly connected with the natural character, it appears as a morality of a determinate kind and of greater liveliness and intensity.
At the same time it is less bound up with the consciousness of duty than morality proper.
zh: 由于美德部分地与自然性情相连，它显得是一种特定样式的道德，并且具有更大的生动性与强度。
同时它同义务意识的联系，也不如道德本身那样紧密。

en: Insofar as man is cultivated, he has the possibility of acting.
Insofar as he really acts, he is necessarily in relation with other men.
The first necessary relation in which the individual enters into relation with others is the family relation.
It indeed also has a legal side, but it is subordinated to the side of moral disposition, of love, and of trust.
zh: 就人受过教养而言，他就有行动的可能。
就他真正行动而言，他必然处于与他人���关系之中。
个体与他人发生关系的第一种必然关系，就是家庭关系。
它固然也有一面法的方面，但这一面从属于道德心态、爱的和信任的那一面。

en: Explanation.
The family essentially makes up only one substance, only one person.
The family members are not persons toward one another.
They enter into such a relation only insofar as the moral bond has been dissolved through a misfortune.
Among the ancients the disposition of family love, acting in its sense, was called pietas.

Pietas has in common with Frömmigkeit, which is also designated by this word, that it presupposes an absolute bond, the unity existing in and for itself in a spiritual substance, a bond that is not tied by particular arbitrariness or chance.
zh: 诠释。
家庭本质上只构成一个实体，只构成一个人格。
家庭成员彼此之间并不是各自独立的人格。
只有当道德的纽带因一场不幸而解开时，他们才进入这样的关系。
在古人那里，家庭之爱的这种心态、按它的意义行事，叫做 pietas。
孝敬与虔诚——后者也用同一个词来称呼——的共同之处在于：它们都预设一条绝对的纽带，即在一个精神实体中自在自为地存在的统一，一条不是由特殊的任意或偶然系在一起的纽带。

en: This disposition consists more precisely in the fact that every member of the family does not have its essence in its own person, but that only the whole of the family constitutes their personality.
zh: 这种心态更确切地说在于：家庭的每一个成员并不把自身的本质置于自身的人格之中，而唯有家庭的整体才构成他们的人格性。

en: The union of persons of the two sexes, which is marriage, is essentially neither merely a natural, animal union nor a mere civil contract, but a moral union of disposition in mutual love and trust, which makes them into one person.
zh: 异性人格之间的结合即是婚姻，它本质上既不只是自然的、兽性的结合，也不只是纯粹的民事契约，而是心态在相互的爱与信任中的一种道德的结合，这种结合使他们成为一个人格。

en: The duty of parents toward children is to provide for their preservation and education, - that of children [to obey them] until they become independent, and to honor them their whole life, - that of siblings as such, to act toward one another according to love and special equity.
zh: 父母对子女的义务是为他们的保存与教育操劳，——子女的义务则是［服从］他们直到自己独立自主为止，并终其一生敬重他们，——兄弟姐妹之间的义务，总的说来，是按爱和格外的公平彼此行事。

en: The natural whole which the family constitutes expands into the whole of a people and a state, in which the individuals have an independent will of their own.
zh: 家庭所构成的这个自然整体，扩展为一个民族和国家的整体；在其中，各个人各自具有独立的意志。

en: Explanation.
The state on the one hand aims at being able to do without the disposition of the citizens, namely insofar as it has to make itself independent of the will of the individuals.
It therefore prescribes precisely their liabilities to the individuals, namely the share which they must perform for the whole.

It cannot rely on disposition alone, because that can just as well be self-interested and can oppose the interest of the state. - In this way the state becomes a machine, a system of external dependencies.
But on the other hand it cannot do without the disposition of the citizens.
The prescription of the government can contain only what is general.
The actual action, the fulfilment of the state’s purposes, contains the particular mode of efficacy.
This can only arise from the individual understanding, from the disposition of man.
zh: 诠释。
国家一方面力求能够不依赖公民的心态，也就是就它必须使自己独立于各个人的意志而言。
所以它准确地规定各个人的责任，也就是他们必须为整体付出的份额。
它不能只依赖心态，因为心态同样可以是自利的，并且可以与国家的利益相对立。——以这种方式，国家就成为一台机器、一个外在依赖的系统。
但另一方面，它也不能没有公民的心态。
政府的训令只能包含普遍的东西。
现实的行动、国家目的之实现，包含着起作用的具体方式。
这只能出自个人的知性、出自人的心态。

en: The state comprehends society not only under legal relations but, as a genuinely higher moral community, mediates the unity in customs, cultivation, and general mode of thinking and acting (in that each surveys and recognizes his own universality in the other in a spiritual way).
zh: 国家不仅在法的关系之下把握社会，而且作为一个真正更高的道德共同体，在习俗、教养以及一般的思维与行动方式上促成一致性（每个人在他人身上以精神的方式观照并认出他自身的普遍性）。

en: In the spirit of a people each single citizen has his spiritual substance.

The preservation of the individuals is founded not only on the preservation of this living whole, but this same whole also constitutes the general spiritual nature or the essence of each one against his particularity.
The preservation of the whole therefore precedes the preservation of the individual, and all shall have this disposition.
zh: 在一个民族的精神中，每一个公民都有他的精神实体。
各个人的保存不仅建立在这个活的整体的保存之上，而且正是这个整体，使每个人那普遍的精神本性、或者其本质，得以抵挡他的个别性。
所以整体的保存先于个人的保存，并且所有人都应当具有这种心态。

en: Considered purely with respect to its legal side, insofar as the state protects the private rights of the individuals and the individual first looks to what is his own, a sacrifice of a part of property against the state is indeed possible in order to preserve the rest.
Patriotism, however, is not founded on this calculation but on the consciousness of the absoluteness of the state.

This disposition, to sacrifice property and life for the whole, is all the greater in a people the more the individuals can act for the whole with their own will and self-activity, and the greater trust they have in it.
(The beautiful patriotism of the Greeks. - Distinction of Bürger as bourgeois and citoyen.)
zh: 单从法的方面看，就国家保护各个人的私权、而个人首先着眼于自己所有的东西而言，为了保住其余部分，对国家牺牲一部分财产确实是可能的。
但爱国主义并不建立在这种计算之上，而是建立在对国家之绝对性的意识之上。
这种为整体牺牲财产与生命的心态，在一个民族中越是各个个能以自己的意志和自主活动为整体行事、并且越是他们对它抱有更大的信任，就越是伟大。
（希腊人的高贵爱国主义。——「Bürger」作为 bourgeois 与 citoyen 的差别。）

en: The disposition of obedience toward the commands of the government, of attachment to the person of the prince and to the constitution, and the feeling of national honour are the virtues of the citizen of every well-ordered state.
zh: 服从政府命令的心态、对君主本人和对宪法的依恋之情以及民族荣誉感，是一个秩序良好的国家的公民的美德。

en: The state does not rest on an express contract of one with all and of all with one, or of the individual with the government; and the general will of the whole is not the expressing will of the individuals but is the absolutely general will which is binding for the individuals in and for itself.
zh: 国家并不建立在「一人与所有人、所有人与一人」或「个人与政府」之间的明文契约之上；并且整体那普遍意志并不是各个人的表达出来的意志，而是自在自为地对各个具有约束力的绝对普遍的意志。

en: The duties toward others are first the legal duties, which must be bound up with the disposition to do right for the sake of right.

The remaining of these duties are founded on the disposition to hold others equal to oneself not only as abstract person but also in their particularity, to consider their weal and woe as one’s own, and to prove this by active help.
zh: 对他人的义务首先是法权义务，它们必须与「为了权利本身而去做」的心态相联结。
这些义务中的其余各项，建立在这样一种心态上：不把他人仅仅当作抽象的人格，而且也当其特殊性而与自己同等看待，把他们的福祉与祸患当作自己的，并通过积极的帮助来证明这一点。

en: This moral way of thinking and acting goes beyond right.
Rectitude, however, the observance of the strict duties toward others, is the first duty which must underlie.
There can be noble and generous actions which are without rectitude.
They then have their ground in self-love and in the consciousness of having done something special, whereas what rectitude demands is a duty valid for all, not an arbitrary one.
zh: 这种道德的思维与行动方式超出了法。
但正直，即对他人严格义务的遵守，是必须作为基础的第一项义务。
可以有高尚而豪爽的行为是不带正直的。
它们于是以自爱和「自己做了点特别的事」这一意识为根据；而正直所要求的则是一项对所有人都有效、并非出于任意的义务。

en: Among the particular duties toward others, truthfulness in speaking and acting is the first.

It consists in the equality of what is and what one is conscious of with that which one expresses and shows toward others. - Untruthfulness is the inequality and the contradiction of the consciousness and of that which one is for others, thus of one’s inner and one’s actuality, and thereby the nullity of oneself.
zh: 在对他人的特殊义务中，言说与行动上的真实性是第一项。
它在于：所是的东西和所意识的东西，同对他人所表达和所显示的东西彼此等同。——不真实则是意识与「自己对于他人是怎样的」之间的不等同与矛盾，因而是自己的内在与自己的现实性之间的不等同与矛盾，并由此成为自身的虚无性。

en: Untruthfulness also belongs pre-eminently to the case in which what one means is supposed to be a good intention or disposition, whereas what one does is something evil.

(This inequality between the disposition and what the action is in itself would at least be a clumsiness, but insofar as the actor is at all guilty, one must take such a one who does evil to mean it as evil too.)
zh: 不真实尤其还包括这样一种情形：一个人心里以为自己是出于好的意图或心态，而他做的事却是恶的。
（这种心态与行为本身之所是之间的不等同，至少还算是一种不灵巧；但就行动者总之有罪责而言，一个做恶事的人必须被认为也是怀着恶念去做它的。）

en: It presupposes a particular relation in order to have the right to tell someone the truth about his conduct.
If one does this without having the right to it, then one is untruthful in that one sets up a relation to the other which does not hold.
zh: 它预设一种特殊的关系，才能有权利把某人的行为举止的真情告诉对方。
如果人这样做而并不具有这种权利，那么他就是不真实的，因为他对对方建立起一种并不成立的关系。

en: Explanation.
For a first thing it is the first thing to say the truth insofar as one knows that it is true.
It is ignoble not to say the truth when it is in its right place to say it, because one thereby degrades oneself before oneself and before the other.
But one also ought not to say the truth when one has no calling for it or not even a right.

If one merely says the truth in order to have done one’s duty, without further success, then it is at least something superfluous, for the point is not that I have said the matter, but that it comes about.
Speaking is not yet the deed or action, which is higher. - The truth is then said in the right place and at the right time when it serves to bring the matter about.
Speech is a remarkably great means, but great understanding is required to use it correctly.
zh: 诠释。
首先，应当说出真相，就人知道它是真实的而言。
在该说真话的地方不说真话，是不高贵的，因为人由此在自己和他人面前贬低了自己。
但如果人对此没有职责、乃至没有权利，也不应当说真话。
如果人说出真相只是为了尽了自己的责任、却没有进一步的效果，那么这至少是一件多余的事，因为关键不在于我说了这件事，而在于事情得以实现。
言说还不是那更高的行为或行动。——当说真话有助于使事情得以实现时，真相就是在恰当的地方、在恰当的时候被说出的。
言说是一个大得出奇的手段，但要正确地使用它，则需要很大的知性。

en: With defamation, which is a real lie, is connected the evil speaking about others, the narration of such things as are detrimental to the honour of a third person and are not manifest to the narrator in and for themselves.
It is accustomed to happen in disapproving zeal against unmoral actions, even with the addition that one could not vouch for the narrations for certain and would have meant to say nothing.

But in this case it is connected with dishonesty, actually spreading the narrations one professes not to want to spread; and in the other case with hypocrisy, wanting to speak morally and actually acting evilly.
zh: 与诽谤——一种真正的谎话——相联系的是恶言中伤，即讲述那些有损于第三者名誉、并且对讲述者本人并非自在自为地显而易见的事情。
这种情形常以义愤的形式针对不合道德的行为发生，甚至还会附带一句：这些讲述不能确定担保，而且自己并没有说什么。
但在前一种情形中，这与不诚实相连：口称不想散播这些讲述，实际上却散播了它们；在后一种情形中，则与伪善相连：想要说道德的话，实际上却做着恶事。

en: Explanation.
Hypocrisy consists in this, that people act evilly but give appearance to others of having a good intention, of wanting to do something good.
But the external action is not different from the internal one.
In an evil deed the intention too was essentially evil and not good.
It can happen in this that man wanted to achieve something good or at least something permissible.
But one cannot in this want to make that which is evil in and for itself a means to something good.
The purpose or the intention does not sanctify the means.
The moral principle has to do primarily with the disposition or with the intention.

But it is just as essential that not only the intention but also the action be good. - Likewise man must not persuade himself that in the ordinary acting of individual life he has important, excellent intentions.

Now as man on the one hand readily ascribes good intentions to his own actions and seeks to make great his actions that are unimportant in and for themselves by reflections, so conversely it happens with others that he wants to ascribe something evil to the great or at least good actions of others through a self-interested intention.
zh: 诠释。
伪善在于：人们做着恶事，却在他人面前装出「怀有好的意图、想要做点好事」的样子。
但外在的行为并不与内在的行为不同。
在一次恶的行为中，意图本质上也是恶的而不是善的。
在这种情况下可能发生的是：人想要达到某个善的东西、或至少是某个被允许的东西。
但人在这种情况下不能想要把自在自为地是恶的东西当成通向某个善的东西的手段。
目的或意图并不能使手段神圣化。
道德原则主要关乎心态或意图。
但同样本质的是：不仅意图要善，行为也必须善。——同样，人也不应当说服自己，以为在个体生活的日常行为中他怀有重要的、卓越的意图。
正如人一方面乐于给自己的行为加上好的意图，并试图通过反思把自己那些自在自为地不重要的行为弄得重大一样，反过来在他人身上也会发生这样的事：他试图用一个自利的意图，把他人重大的、或至少是好的行为加上某种恶的东西。

en: The disposition to harm others knowingly and wilfully is evil.
The disposition which permits itself, out of weakness for its inclination, to violate duties toward others and also toward itself is bad.
zh: 明知故犯地存心伤害他人的心态是恶的。
那种出于对自身倾向的软弱而容许自己违反对他人、乃至对自己的义务的心态，是不善的。

en: Explanation.
To the good there stands opposed the evil, but also the bad.
Evil contains the fact that it occurs with resolve of the will.
It thus has in advance of the bad the formal, a strength of will, which is also the condition of the good.
The bad, on the contrary, is something without will.
The bad man follows his inclination and thereby neglects duties.
It would be fitting for the bad man as well if the duties were fulfilled; only he does not have the will to master his inclinations or habits.
zh: 诠释。
与善相对立的是恶，但也有不善。
恶包含着：它是以意志的决断而发生的。
所以与不善相比，恶预先具有那形式性的东西，即意志的一种力量，而这同样是善的条件。
相反，不善是某种没有意志的东西。
行不善者顺着自己的倾向行事，并因此疏忽了义务。
即便义务得到履行，对行不善者来说也是恰当的；只是他没有意志去制服自己的倾向或习惯。

en: Which services we have to render or are able to render to other men depends on the contingent relations in which we stand toward them and on the particular circumstances in which we ourselves find ourselves.
If we are able to render a service to someone, we have only this, that he is a human being, and to consider his distress.
zh: 我们应当或能够向他人提供哪些效劳，取决于我们同他们所处的那种偶然的关系，以及我们自己所处的那种特殊的情境。
如果我们能够为某人提供一件效劳，那么我们所要依据的就只有这一点：他是一个人，并且要把他的困苦看在眼里。

en: Explanation.
The first condition for rendering help to others consists in this, that we have a right to it, namely to consider them as those in distress and to act toward them as such.
The help must therefore occur with their will.
This presupposes a certain acquaintance or familiarity.
The person in need is as such unequal to the person not in need.
It therefore depends on his will whether he wants to appear as one in need.

He will want this if he is convinced that I treat and regard him, notwithstanding this inequality, as one equal to me. - Secondly, I must have the means at hand to help him. - Finally, there can also be cases in which his distress is evident and in it there lies as it were the declaration of his will that help be rendered to him.
zh: 诠释。
为他人提供帮助的第一个条件在于：我们对此拥有权利，也就是把他们看作受困苦的人，并以此对他们行事。
所以帮助必须得到他们的同意而发生。
这预设一定的相识或亲近。
有需要的人作为这样的人，与没有需要的人是不等同的。
所以他是否愿意作为一个有需要的人出现，取决于他的意志。
如果他确信：尽管存在这种不等同，我仍把他当作与我同等的人来对待和看待，他就会愿意这样做。——其次，我必须手里有能够帮助他的手段。——最后，也可能有这样一些情形：他的困苦是明显的，其中仿佛就包含着他「要人们帮助他」这一意志的宣告。

en: The duty of general human love extends more precisely to those with whom we stand in the relation of acquaintance and friendship.
The original unity of men must have been voluntarily made into such closer connections, through which more determinate duties arise.
zh: 普遍的人道之爱的义务，更确切地说延伸到那些我们同他们处于相识与友谊关系之中的人。
人的原初统一必须是自愿地被做成这样一些更切近的联系，通过这些联系就产生了更具体的义务。

en: (Friendship rests on the equality of characters, especially of the interest in doing a common work together, not on the pleasure in the person of the other as such.
One must be as little a burden to one’s friends as possible.
To demand services from friends is the most delicate of all.
One must not spare oneself the thing in order to lay it on others.)
zh: （友谊建立在性情、尤其是「一起做一件共同事业」这一利害关系的等同上，而不是建立在对「他人其人」的快乐上。
人必须尽可能少给自己的朋友添麻烦。
向朋友索取效劳，是最微妙不过的。
人不可为了把事情推给他人，而自己逃避这件事。）

en: The duty of prudence appears at first as a duty toward oneself in the relations to others, insofar as self-interest is the purpose. - But the true own benefit is essentially achieved through ethical conduct, which is thus the true prudence.
It is at the same time contained therein that with respect to moral conduct the own benefit can indeed be a consequence, but is not to be regarded as the purpose.
zh: 精明的义务起初表现为在与他人的关系中对自己的一项义务，就自利是目的而言。——但真正的自身利益在本质上是通过伦理的行为才达到的，而这种伦理的行为因而就是真正的精明。
其中同时包含着：就道德的行为而言，自身利益固然可能是后果，但不可把它看作目的。

en: Insofar as the own benefit does not lie immediately in moral conduct and depends on the particular, contingent in the whole, benevolence of others, one is here in the sphere of mere inclinations toward one another, and prudence consists in not injuring the inclinations of others and preserving them for oneself.

But even in this respect, what brings benefit is in fact also what belongs to it in and for itself, namely to let others alone where we have neither duty nor right to disturb them and to win their inclination through our conduct.
zh: 就自身利益并不直接寓于道德的行为之中、而依赖于他人那特殊而就整体而言偶然的善意而言，人在这里就处在彼此纯粹好感的领域之中，而精明就在于不伤害他人的倾向、并为自己保有它们。
但即使在这种考量之下，带来益处的东西其实也就是那自在自为地属于它的东西，即：在我们既无义务也无权利去打扰他人的地方，任由他们，并通过我们的行为去赢得他们的好感。

en: Politeness is the manifestation of benevolent dispositions, also of services, especially toward those with whom we do not yet stand in a closer relation of acquaintance or friendship.
It is falseness if this manifestation is combined with the opposite dispositions.

True politeness, however, is to be regarded as a duty, because we should have benevolent dispositions toward one another in general, in order to open through the manifestation of them the way to closer connections with them.
zh: 客气是善意的心态、甚至也是效劳的表现，尤其是对我们尚未与之处于更切近的相识或友谊关系之中的人。
如果这种表现与相反的心态连在一起，它就是虚伪。
但真正的客气应被看作一项义务，因为我们就总体而言本就应当彼此怀有善意的心态，以便通过这种表现，为与他们建立更切近的联系开辟道路。

en: (To render a service, a courtesy, something agreeable to a stranger is politeness.
The same, however, we should also render to an acquaintance or a friend.
Toward strangers and those with whom we do not stand in closer connection, it is a matter of the appearance of benevolence and of nothing but this appearance.
Finesse, delicacy is not to do or say anything which the relation does not permit. - Greek humanity and urbanity in Socrates and Plato.)
zh: （为一个陌生人提供一件效劳、给一个方便、带来一点令人愉快的东西，这就是客气。
不过，同样的事我们也应当为一个熟人或朋友去做。
对陌生人以及那些我们与之并无更切近联系的人，重要的只是善意的假象，此外别无他物。
精细、体贴，就是不去做或说关系所不容许的事。——苏格拉底与柏拉图身上希腊的人道与风度。）

80.zh: 第三部分 宗教学说

en: The moral law in us is the eternal law of reason, which we must honour irresistibly and through which we feel ourselves bound indissolubly.
But we equally immediately see the inadequacy of our individuality to it, recognize it as something higher than we are, as an independent, self-standing, absolute being.
zh: 我们内心的道德法则就是那永恒的理性法则：我们必须不可抗拒地敬重它，并且通过它感到自己不可解除地与之相连。
但我们同样直接地看出我们的个体性同它不相宜，认出它是一个高于我们、比我们更高的事物，是一个不依赖我们、独立自在的绝对存在者。

en: This absolute being is present in our pure consciousness and reveals itself to us therein.
The knowledge of it, as mediated through it in us, is immediate for us and can in that respect be called faith.
zh: 这个绝对存在者当下就在我们纯粹的意识中，并在其中向我们显现自身。
对它的知识，就它在我们之中借它为中介而言，对我们来说是直接的，因此可以称之为信仰。

en: The elevation above the sensuous and the finite indeed cancels, on our side, the mediation of this knowledge, but only insofar as one has started out from the sensuous and finite yet at the same time leaves it and recognizes it in its nullity.

But this knowledge of the absolute is itself an absolute and immediate knowledge and cannot have something finite as its positive ground or be mediated through something which it is not itself as a proof.
zh: 对感性的与有限之物的提升，就我们这一方而言，固然否定地取消了对这一知识的中介；但仅仅是这样一种情形：人虽从感性的和有限之物出发，却同时离开它并在它的虚无性中认出它。
但这一关于绝对者的知识本身就是一种绝对而直接的知识，它不能把某个有限之物作为自己的肯定根据，也不能通过某个不是它自身的东西来中介、作为证明。

en: This knowledge must determine itself more precisely and not remain an inner feeling, a faith in the undetermined being as such, but become a cognition of it.

The cognition of God is not mediated through reason - for reason is only a reflex of God and is essentially the knowledge of the absolute -, but that cognition is mediated only through the understanding, the knowledge of the finite and relative.
zh: 这一知识必须进一步得到规定，不能停留在内心感觉、对那无规定的存在者的信仰上，而必须成为对它的认识。
对上帝的认识并不是通过理性为中介的——因为理性不过是上帝的假象，本质上是对绝对者的知识——而那种认识只是通过知性为中介，即通过对有限者与相对者的知识。

en: Religion itself consists in the occupation of feeling and thought with the absolute being and in the actualization of its representation, with which the self-forgetfulness of its particularity in this elevation and the acting in this sense, with a view to the absolute being, is necessarily connected.
zh: 宗教本身在于感觉与思想对绝对存在者的经营，以及把它的表象当下化；而在这种提升中它自身特殊性的自我遗忘、以及顾及绝对存在者而按这一意义行动，是与之必然联系在一起的。

en: God is the absolute spirit, i.e. he is the pure being which makes itself its object, but therein merely surveys itself, or in its becoming-other returns outright into itself and is equal to itself.
zh: 上帝是绝对的精神，也就是说，它是那个把自己变成对象的纯粹存在者，但在其中只是观照自己，或者在自己的成为他者的过程中彻底地回到自身，并与自身等同。

en: God is, according to the moments of his being, 1. absolutely holy, insofar as he is the being that is simply universal in himself.
He is 2. absolute power, insofar as he realizes the universal and preserves the particular in the universal, or eternal creator of the universe.
He is 3.
wisdom, insofar as his power is only holy power, 4.
goodness, insofar as he lets the particular have its actuality, and 5.
justice, insofar as he brings it back to the universal eternally.
zh: 上帝按其存在的诸环节而言：1. 是绝对神圣的，就它是自在地、无条件地普遍的那个存在者而言。
2. 是绝对的威力，就他实现普遍者、并在普遍者中保存个别者而言，或者是宇宙永恒的创造者。
是智慧，就他的威力只是神圣的威力而言；4.
是良善，就他让个别者得以有其现实性而言；以及 5.
是公正，就他把它永恒地带回到普遍者之中而言。

en: Evil is the estrangement from God, insofar as the particular according to its freedom separates itself from the universal and in the exclusion from it strives to be absolutely for itself.
Insofar as it is the nature of the finite free being to reflect itself into this particularity, it is to be regarded as evil.
zh: 恶是与上帝的异化，就个别者依其自由而与普遍者分离、并且在对普遍者的排除中力图绝对地为自己而存在而言。
就有限自由存在者的本性在于把自身反映到这一个别性之中而言，它应当被视为恶的。

en: But the freedom of the individual being is at the same time in itself an equality of the being with itself, or it is in itself of divine nature.

This cognition that human nature is not truly something alien to the divine nature assures men of divine grace and lets them grasp it, through which the reconciliation of God with the world, or the disappearance of their estrangement from God, comes about.
zh: 但个别存在者的自由同时自在地就是该存在者与自身的等同，或者说，它自在地具有上帝的本性。
「人的本性并非真正是与上帝的本性相对的他物」这一认识，使人确信上帝的恩典，并使人抓住这恩典；由此便有了上帝与世界的和解，或者说，他们同上帝的异化便消失了。

en: Divine service is the determinate occupation of thought and feeling with God, through which the individual strives to bring about its unity with him and to give itself the consciousness and assurance of this unity, a correspondence of its will with the divine will which it is to prove through the disposition and mode of conduct of its actual life.
zh: 敬拜是思想与感受对上帝的规定性经营，个体借此力求造成它与上帝的一致，并给自己以这种一致的意识与确信；这种其意志与神圣意志的相合，它应当通过其现实生活的心态与行为方式来证明。

101.en: 9. Doctrine of Religion for the Middle and Upper Classes77)
101.zh: 9. 中等阶级与上层阶级的宗教学说77)

en: Okt.
Relig.
feeling; Philos.
Theology; cult; life.
The ancients [regarded] nature, sun, sea, as higher natures than [that of] men - Titans, afterward Greek gods; consciousness of the essence of their own.
zh: 宗教：
感受；哲学。
神学；崇拜；生活。
古人［认为］自然、太阳、海洋是比人的本性更高的本性——提坦，以及后来的希腊诸神；其自身的本质的意识。

en: Philosophy strove to prove the existence of God and the origin of evil, theodicy, - to justify evil and to reconcile the freedom of man with divine justice.
zh: 哲学曾致力于证明上帝的存在与恶的来源，即神义论，——为恶辩护，并把人的自由与神圣的公正相协调。

en: Temporal, external, fates, occurrences, action, finite nature - elevation above it into a region where all these contradictions are dissolved, all inequality is equalized, all the tears of suffering are dried, all wishes are satisfied, through elevation above it -
zh: 时间的、外在的、命运、事件、行动、有限的本性——经由对它们的提升而进入一个这样的区域：在那里这一切矛盾都得到消解，一切不同都得到持平，一切苦难的眼泪都擦干，一切愿望都得到满足——

en: Nature, its connection, things fitting into one another, purposiveness, - there is a creator; an original unity. - The appearances of nature are received without thought, [not because they are] thoughtless for us, - but a friendly being offers them to us.
zh: 自然、它的关联、互相嵌合、合目的性——有一位创造者；一种原初的统一。——自然的现象被无思地接受着，［不是因为它们］对我们来说是无思的——而是一个友善的存在者把它们递到我们面前。

en: Still more in human fates, disconnected, contradiction, - concept of right and merit.
zh: 在人的命运中更是如此，没有关联，矛盾——法与功绩的概念。

en: Efficacy, actuality of our doing and dealing; - idea great in the individual, not his own - his power is insignificant to carry it out.
Connection of his willing and the free actuality into which he puts his deed; own laws and course of nature, another influence.
zh: 我们所为之事的效果、实在性；——观念在个体中是伟大的，却不是他自己的——他的力量微不足道，不足以实行它。
他的意愿与他把自己行动置入其中的自由现实性之间的关联；自己的规律和自然的进程，另一种作用。

en: Knowledge of the absolute being as his own; cult, consciousness of unification with it.
Service toward a lord who wants arbitrary, unintelligible commands carried out; - toward a gracious lord, whom we make favourable to us by service; always a foreign purpose, foreign benefit -
zh: 对绝对存在者的知识，把它当作自己的；崇拜，与它合一而为一的意识。
对一个想要任意的、无法理解命令得到执行的主人的效劳；——对一个仁慈的主人，我们通过效劳来博取他的欢心；总是一个异己的目的、异己的利益——

en: Spirit in itself.
zh: 自在的精神。

en: Proof through the form of the inference (from the known to the unknown).
The existence of God [is] not equal to the existence of a temporal thing, but rather his existence is the cancelling of all other existences.
The truth of everything; everything returns into it as into its ground.
Inference from one positive to another positive.
zh: 通过推论的形式所作的证明（从已知者到未知者）。
上帝的存在［不］等于一个时间性事物的存在，而毋宁说他的存在就是对一切其它存在的扬弃。
一切的真理；一切作为返回于自己的根据之中。
从一个肯定者推论到另一个肯定者。

en: Inference: Because we have a need for religion, something must exist that corresponds to this drive; from the subjective to the objective.
zh: 推论：因为我们有宗教的需要，所以必定有某种与这一冲动相应的东西存在；从主观者到客观者。

en: The need for religion is the feeling of the nullity of the temporal world-being and of oneself in its particularity, the immersion of it into the being, and the preservation of oneself therein.
zh: 宗教的需要是对时间性的世界存在者、以及对它自身在其个别性之中的虚无性的感觉，是把它沉浸于本质之中，并因此保全自身。

en: One must regard what is not in its temporal, common actuality but in its truth; - just as man apprehends himself; he receives a consciousness of his being.
zh: 人们必须不是在其时间的、普通的现实性之中、而是在其真理之中看待那所是的；——正如人把握自己；他由此获得对其存在的意识。

en: The ancients - their being as nature
zh: 古人——他们的本质作为自然

en: Basic ideas of the Orientals; pure light
zh: 东方人的基本观念；纯粹的光

en: From the order - therefore an ordering one
zh: 从秩序而来——所以有一位安排者

en: From the disorder - the same
zh: 从无序而来——同样如此

en: In the proofs of the existence of God there are always two kinds of actuality: the foreign - that of the senses or of self-consciousness, - and the actuality of God, as an other-worldly one.
World-soul of nature; if nature, as it is, is a valid actuality, - a fixed one
zh: 在关于上帝定在的证明中，总有两大类现实性：异己的现实性——感性的或自我意识的，——与上帝的现实性，作为一种彼岸的现实性。
自然的世界灵魂；如果自然如其本然地是一种有效的现实性——一种固定的现实性

en: God alone the truly actual
zh: 唯上帝是真正现实的

en: An inferred actuality and one contemplated.
To true actuality both belong.
zh: 一种推论出来的现实性和一种直观到的现实性。
真正的现实性两者兼有。

en: Negative elevation to God; flight of the sufferer and the unfortunate out of the world, out of misery [and] wickedness.
zh: 向上帝的否定性提升；受苦者与不幸者从世界、从苦难［和］卑劣中逃出。

en: Positive elevation - that of thankfulness, of beauty - the happy are not pious.
zh: 肯定性的提升——感恩的提升、美的提升——幸福的人并不虔诚。

en: The truth of the world is not this immediate appearance, not this immediate determinate being, but it is the disappearing, the self-cancelling and the going back into its being; in external nature, in the inner nature of man.78
zh: 世界的真理不是这种直接的现象，不是这种直接的定在，而是它的消失、自行扬弃与返回其本质；在外在的自然中，在人的内在本性中。78）

en: How must we represent this absolute being to ourselves; which determinations [has it]?
zh: 我们应当如何表象这一绝对存在者；它有［怎样］的规定？

en: God infinite being, i.e. that finitude does not remain beyond as a true world; but that the finite disappears to the spirit as truth, that he holds only the being to be the actual. - Plato.
Idea the supersensuous.
zh: 上帝是无限的存在者，也就是说，有限性并不作为一个真的世界留在彼岸；而是有限性对精神来说作为真理而消失，他只把本质者视为现实的。——柏拉图。
观念 超感性之物。

en: 79) α) Sensuous cognition, β) reflected; thoughts, determinations of reflection - power; the inner is not in and for itself, but it is always inferred from its determinate being back to it, from the finite to the infinite. γ) Absolute mode of cognition; the world only appearance; God the being; in itself. - God is the pure life in all life, the pure spirit in all spirit.
One must not come to the idea of God and then to his determinate being.
zh: 79) α) 感性的认识，β) 反思的认识；思想、反思的规定——力；内在的东西不是自在自为的，而只是不断从它的定在回到它那里，从有限者到无限者。γ) 绝对的认识方式；世界只是现象；上帝是本质；自在。——上帝是一切生命中的纯粹生命，一切精神中的纯粹精神。
不可以先达到上帝的观念、然后再达到他的定在。

en: World only an aggregate of the finite.
zh: 世界只是有限者的聚合体。

en: Being the living, real unity - (examples e.g. the germ, the spirit which contains all ideas in itself; actual -
zh: 本质是活的、实在的统一——（例如种子、在其自身中包含一切观念的精神；现实的——

en: The being is the actual itself; its idea is not separated from its existence; - not an idea like a thing of representation or imagination, - arbitrary, but absolutely necessary, - unity of possibility and actuality. - God is the being of the world, of the outer world and of ourselves; whether it also be - i.e. outside our representation; like house, tree, stars; - so God is not a single, sensuous, external being.
zh: 本质就是现实者本身；它的观念并不与它的存在相分离；——不是像表象或想象的事物那样的一个观念，——不是任意的，而是绝对必然的，——是可能与现实性的统一。——上帝是世界的本质，是外在世界和我们自身的本质；无论它是否也在——即在我们的表象之外；如房屋、树木、星辰；——所以上帝不是一个个别的、感性的、外在的存在。

en: We are, and a thought is a moment in us, but we do not have reason, rather reason has us.
So we do not have the thought of God, but this our temporal, divided thinking is immersed in him; - such a thinking as separated idea and being, possibility and actuality, is nothing true.80)
zh: 我们存在，而思想是我们中的一个环节，但并不是我们拥有理性，而是理性拥有我们。
所以我们并不拥有上帝的思想，而是我们这种时间的、分离着的思维沉浸在他之中；——这样一种把观念与存在、可能性与现实性分离开来的思维，不是任何真的东西。80)

en: Proofs of the existence of God.
God all actuality.
Actuality is no predicate that comes to the concept, i.e. to the content, as an addition.81)
zh: 关于上帝定在的证明。
上帝是一切实在性。
实在性并不是一个附加到概念之上、即附加到内容之上的谓词。81)

en: Kant [Critique of Pure Reason, B, page] 658 - "although in my concept of the possible real content of a thing in general nothing is missing, yet something is still missing in the relation to my whole state of thinking, namely that the cognition of that object also be possible a posteriori."
zh: 康德［《纯粹理性批判》B 版第］658 页——“虽然在我关于一个一般事物的可能实在内容的概念上并无欠缺，但在我思维的整体状态的关系上还缺少点什么，即对该对象的认识也可以是后天的（a posteriori）。”

en: Kosmol[ogical proof] starts from experience that something exists, infers [to] absolute necessity - from the contingent to the cause - form of finitude, experience, sensuousness - because the cause itself is finite; - the cause conditioned through being.82)
zh: 宇宙论［证明］从经验出发，即某物存在，推论［出］绝对的必然性——从偶然者到原因——是有限性、经验、感性的形式——因为原因本身是有限的；——原因通过存在而受条件限制。82）

en: Physikoteleolog[ical proof] - Kant only the form of things, arrangement, not substance.
zh: 物理神学［证明］——康德只讲事物的形式、布置，不讲实体。

en: - a proportionate cause; this content purpose - again cannot infer to a cause from the purpose - an idle content -83)
zh: ——一个相称的原因；这内容是目的——又不可从目的推论到原因——一个空洞的内容——83）

en: Cognition is not an inference from an existence; God in connection with the existence.
Rather one cognizes existence, i.e. cognizes its finitude, cognizes the infinite, the eternal, the rational in it.
God is the being in all existence; the divine therein; the life in all living; the reason in all rational, the infinite in all finite - the essence.
All existence is becoming, that which unites itself is the essence; - All ...
zh: 认识不是从一个定在所作的推论；上帝是同定在相关联的。
而是认识定在，也就是认识它的有限性，认识那内在于它的无限者、永恒者、理性者。
上帝是一切定在中的存在；其中神圣的东西；一切有生命者中的生命；一切有理性的东西中的理性，一切有限者中的无限者——即本质。
一切定在都是生成，那使自身合而为一的就是本质；——一切……

en: God first as being - the infinite, of the finite
zh: 上帝首先是存在——无限者，有限者的……

en: β) Being, substance, connected in contingency - the power and blind necessity84)
zh: β) 本质、实体，在偶然性中相互关联着——那威力与盲目的必然性84）

en: γ) the universal, the concept of everything; the absolute subject, life, world-soul and intelligence, spirit, - nothing lower than reason.
zh: γ) 普遍者、一切的概念；绝对的主体、生命、世界灵魂与理智、精神，——没有什么比理性更低。

en: I. Being of God; all things [go] back into it and come forth from it - the ground is the truth - the sensuous way of thinking stands opposed to this.
zh: 一、上帝的存在；一切事物都返回于它、并从它产生——根据就是真理——感性的思维方式与此相对立。

en: II.
Concept.
Being.
zh: 二、
概念。
存在。

en: III.
Its shape, religion.
zh: 三、
它的形态，宗教。

en: God is 1. the being in all being, the simple first and immediate.
This being is only the abstraction from all determinacy, the undetermined, the motionless.85)
zh: 上帝 1. 是一切存在中的存在，是单纯的、第一的、直接的东西。
这一存在只是对一切规定性的抽象，是不定者、不动者。85)

en: Being is being.
Pure being is namely not the external negation of all determinacy, but in it itself it is the simple, the negative relation to itself; self-determining reflection.
zh: 存在就是本质。
纯粹的存在并不是对一切规定性的外在否定，而是在它自身就是那单纯的、对自身的否定关系；自己规定自己的反思。

en: Being shines in itself; it is the ground of existence and appears; it reveals itself as absolute substance.86)
zh: 本质在自身中映现；它是存在的根据并且显现；它把自己显现为绝对的实体。86）

en: The absolute substance is the immediate unity of reflection in itself and of shining in another or, in other determinations, the unity of thinking and being, so that everything that separates itself from it as an individual thinking or existing being is only a selfless moment or accident of the one substance.
zh: 绝对实体是自身内的反思与在他人中映现的直接统一，或者说，用另外的规定说，是思维与存在的统一；以致一切作为个别思维者或个别存在者而与它相分离的东西，只是那唯一实体的一个无自身的环节或偶性。

en: Substance is power and necessity.
As reflection it is the distinguishing of itself from itself and the subsistence of different things, - the absolute goodness.

But particular things are only transient, each thing is a different one, as separated from the whole; but its subsistence is the whole, and it has at the same time its necessity in that; it returns into its dissolution, - the absolute justice.
zh: 实体是威力与必然性。
作为反思，它是自己与自己的区分，是不同事物的持存——绝对的良善。
但特殊的事物只是暂时的，每一个事物都是一个不同的事物，作为同整体相分离者；但它的持存就是整体，并且它同时在其中有自己的必然性；它返回到自己的消解之中——绝对的公正。

en: Insofar as God is grasped only as substance, he has no existence distinguished from his accidental actuality; just as conversely the particular is only in itself, not however a whole for itself, not a self-being at all in its individuality.
God is in this determination blind necessity without purpose and will.
zh: 就上帝只被把握为实体而言，他没有一种同他偶性的现实性相区别的存在；反过来，个别者也只是自在的，却不是为它自身的整体，根本不是在它的个别性中一个自我存在者。
上帝在这一规定中是无目的、无意志的盲目必然性。

en: God is subject; he is the omnipresent universal being or the substance of everything, but has equally an existence of its own, free of its accidentality, in which he is in and for itself and spirit.
zh: 上帝是主体；他是无所不在的普遍存在者、或一切的实体，但也同样有一种摆脱其偶性的、特有的存在，他在其中自在自为地就是精神。

en: God is the absolute spirit; only insofar is the existence of the world not merely his appearance - it appears, it is not as he is in and for itself, but in his other-being -, but creation.
That God is spirit and creator makes up his fundamental concept.
zh: 上帝是绝对的精神；只有这样，世界的存在才不只是他的现象——他显现，他并不像他自在自为地所是的那样存在，而是在他的他在中，——而是创造。
上帝是精神、是创造者，这构成他的基本概念。

en: The creative power of the spirit consists in this, that it is in and for itself and at the same time, against its being-in-itself, is for itself, that it determines its self-equal substance, in which it has the matter, as the negative of it, as the external, and relates itself to it as absolute subject.
zh: 精神的创造威力在于：它自在自为地存在着，同时针对它的自在存在而为它自身存在着，它把那种它据有物质的、与自身相同的实体规定为它的否定者、规定为外在者，并作为绝对的主体与之相关联。

en: As creation, as the one side of the absolute activity of God, is the negative relation of God to his being and he thereby sets the other of himself, so he is equally the negative relation to this other and the eternal reconciliation of it with itself, the contemplation of it as his own, or the eternal love.
zh: 正如创造作为上帝绝对行动的一面，是上帝对其本质的否定关系，他由此设定出他自己的他者，他也同样是对这一他者的否定关系，是它与自身的永恒和解、把它作为自己的东西来观照，即永恒的爱。

en: The freedom of man and the evil in the world belong to the created nature and express its own estrangement or its negative nature against the divine being; only the spirit is capable of freedom, and God can love the world only in the world of spirits which turns to him through its own determination.
zh: 人的自由和世界中的恶属于被创造的本性，并表达它自身的异化、或它对神圣存在者的否定的本性；只有精神才有能力获得自由，而上帝只能爱那个通过自己的规定转向他的精神世界。

en: Men [can be] tormented by unhappy [?]
spirits - happiness not the goal of the finite. The natural being is the evil; and opposition against the spirit.
Men must represent nature to themselves as evil; the evil is present, not through them. - Not: men must be evil.
Because I am a man, however, I want to praise God.
Necessity - not a spur to activity.
zh: 人［可以］被不幸的［精灵？］
折磨——至福不是有限者的目标。自然的存在是恶的；并且是与精神对立。
人必须把自然表象为恶的；恶存在着，却不是通过他们。——并不是：人必须是恶的。
但因为我是一个人，所以我要赞美上帝。
必然性——不是行动的刺激。

en: Religion is the manner in which man becomes conscious of the divine being, determines its determinate being for himself, and seeks and produces unity with it.
It is the highest consciousness of the spirit, and all other consciousness of it is dependent on this.
zh: 宗教是人借以意识到神圣存在者、规定它的定在、并寻求和造成与它一致的方式。
它是精神的最高意识，其它一切对它的意识都依赖于它。

en: [It] is a relation of man to God; but just as much of God to man.
The determinate being of God: God has determinate being only in religion - objective religion.
zh: ［它］是人与上帝的关系；但同样也是上帝对人的关系。
上帝的定在：上帝只在宗教中才有定在——客观的宗教。

en: The simple concept of the being of God which underlies religion is shapeless.
The further formation of religion consists in cognizing the divine being in its real shape; but this is God as spirit.
zh: 作为宗教之基础的上帝本质的单纯概念是无形态的。
宗教的进一步教化在于：认识那神圣存在者的实在形态；但这形态就是作为精神的上帝。

en: How God is in consciousness, this is the manner of its determinate being; conduct toward others
zh: 上帝如何存在于意识中，这就是他定在的方式；对他者的行为

en: The simplest religion is the veneration of God as an imageless being, which is one and exalted above all determinate being, which has on it not its shape but only a vanishing accident.
zh: 最简单的宗教是把上帝当作一个无形象的存在者来崇敬，它是「一」并且超出于一切规定的定在之上，它在这个定在上没有自己的形态，而只有一个正在消逝的偶性。

en: Appearance in the fiery bush. God who however does not love all men; as subject all the more restricted. Bacchic frenzy of nature. Immediate determinate being.
Worship of the stars. Emanation
zh: 在燃烧的荆棘中显现。上帝并不爱所有人；作为主体则越发受限制。自然的酒神狂迷。直接的定在。
星辰崇拜 流溢

en: To the being in its simplicity actuality opposes itself as a principle independent of it, the original matter or also the evil principle.
zh: 与单纯的本质相对立，现实性把自己表现为一个不依赖于它的原则，即原始的物质或恶的原则。

en: Insofar as the simple being has a determinate being in it, it can have only a simple determinate being and is venerated as one of the simple natural beings.
zh: 就单纯的本质在它自身有一个定在而言，它只能有一个单纯的定在，并作为单纯自然存在者之一而受崇敬。

en: The religion of art shapes the divine being for representation and contains the transition that it has a determinate being not only as a natural being but as the spirits of the peoples and as the particular ethical powers, over which however the simple power of the being hovers as an incomprehensible fate.
zh: 艺术的宗教把神圣存在者塑造给表象，并包含着这样的过渡：它不只是作为自然存在者、而且作为各民族的精神和特殊的伦理力量而具有一个现实的定在；但在这些东西之上，还悬着本质的单纯威力，作为一种不可把握的命运。

en: still does not absolutely unite the particular with the universal.
Mourning.
Beautiful religion.
The Greek religion brought the divine being closer to man.
"When the gods were more human, men too were more divine."
zh: 还没有把个别者与普遍者绝对地结合起来。
悲哀。
美的宗教。
希腊的宗教把神圣存在者带到离人更近的地方。
「当诸神还更有人的样子时，人也更有神的样子。」

en: The spiritual religion finally contains the reconciliation of the world with God and the representation of it in a human shape, namely the consciousness that God is not something alien to man, but that in man he gives the contemplation of himself.
zh: 精神的宗教最终包含着世界与上帝的和解，以及他在人的形象中的表现；也就是这样一种意识：上帝对人来说并不是一个异己的东西，而是在人之中给出对它自身的观照。

en: Evil overcome; l[aw and] nature evil, - providence.
zh: 恶被克服；法［与］自然是恶的，——护佑。
